Descriptive statistics

Words: 155 Articles: 3
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
Descriptive statistics summarizes observed data, for example through location and spread statistics or graphical summaries such as a histogram.

Scatter plot

Words: 36
Descriptive statistics OurBigBook.com
A scatter plot represents paired quantitative observations as points in a coordinate plane. Group labels, uncertainty and transformations can reveal nonlinear patterns or heterogeneous associations that a single correlation coefficient conceals. A visual association does not establish causation.

Box plot

Words: 50
Descriptive statistics OurBigBook.com
A box plot displays a median and interquartile interval, with whiskers and separately marked points according to a stated rule. Common whiskers extend to the most extreme observations within 1.5 interquartile ranges of the box. It compares location, spread and unusually distant observations across groups; whiskers need not represent the full range.

Histogram

Words: 50
Descriptive statistics OurBigBook.com
A histogram groups observations into bins and displays the bin counts or frequencies. For a probability density function estimate, the height in a bin of width δ is its sample count divided by nδ, so each bar's area is the observed relative frequency. This scaling ensures that the histogram integrates to one.

Birthday problem

Words: 60
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
For n independent uniform draws from m labels, the probability of all labels being distinct is ∏j=0n−1​(1−j/m) when n≤m, and zero otherwise. Applying 1−x≤e−x gives a collision probability at least 1−exp[−n(n−1)/(2m)]. The transition therefore occurs at sample size of order m​, not m: many pairs can collide before many labels have been sampled.

Q-Q plot

Words: 61 Articles: 1
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
A quantile-quantile plot compares ordered observations with quantiles of a reference distribution, or with quantiles of another sample. Approximate linearity supports agreement up to location and scale. A regression normal Q-Q plot compares ordered standardized regression residuals with standard normal distribution quantiles.

Normal Q-Q plot

Words: 27
Q-Q plot OurBigBook.com
A Q-Q plot comparing ordered observations with quantiles of a normal distribution. Approximate linearity supports a normal location-scale shape, while systematic curvature reveals deviations such as heavy tails or asymmetry.

Change-point detection

Words: 421 Articles: 6
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
Change-point detection estimates locations where a sequence's distribution or mean changes. A piecewise-constant mean has a sparse vector of adjacent differences; one-dimensional total variation denoising exploits this sparsity without fixing the number of changes in advance.

Poisson count change-point model with gamma priors (p(λ,ϕ,m∣x)∝λα+Sm​−1e−(β+m)λϕγ+SN​−Sm​−1e−(δ+N−m)ϕ)

Words: 174 Articles: 2
Change-point detection OurBigBook.com
For independent Poisson distributions with rate λ up to an unknown index m and rate ϕ after it, independent shape-rate Gamma distribution priors give the displayed posterior distribution when m is uniform on {1,…,N} and Sm​=∑i≤m​xi​. The model differs from a continuous-time Poisson change-point posterior. The endpoint m=N represents no observed change: the second segment is empty and its rate keeps its prior law.

Marginal posterior weights of a Poisson count change point (wm​=(β+m)α+Sm​(δ+N−m)γ+SN​−Sm​Γ(α+Sm​)Γ(γ+SN​−Sm​)​)

Words: 61
Poisson count change-point model with gamma priors OurBigBook.com
Integrating the two rates out of the Poisson count change-point model with gamma priors gives these weights up to a common factor, by the defining Gamma function integral. Normalizing across the finitely many possible indices gives the exact marginal posterior distribution of m, providing a check on Markov chain Monte Carlo estimates. One can also draw m from these weights and then draw both rates from their conditional Gamma distributions, producing independent exact joint posterior samples.

Gibbs updates for a Poisson count change point

Words: 55
Poisson count change-point model with gamma priors OurBigBook.com
The full conditional distributions are λ∣m,x∼Gamma(α+Sm​,β+m) and ϕ∣m,x∼Gamma(γ+SN​−Sm​,δ+N−m), in shape-rate notation. Conditional on the two rates, m has weights wj​=exp[j(ϕ−λ)+Sj​log(λ/ϕ)]. A Gibbs sampler cycles through these three draws. Each update preserves the joint posterior distribution; subtracting the largest log weight before exponentiation stabilizes the categorical draw. Averages of 1{m=N}​ estimate the posterior probability of no observed change.

Gaussian change-point posterior with proper priors (p(θ,ϕ,v,m∣x)∝v−n/2e−Sm​/(2v)p(θ)p(ϕ)p(v)p(m))

Words: 147 Articles: 1
Change-point detection OurBigBook.com
Take independent proper normal prior distributions for the two segment means and a proper inverse-gamma distribution for the common variance. A uniform prior distribution over m=1,…,n may then retain the empty second segment. The posterior distribution is proper: its likelihood function is bounded above by (2π)−n/2v−n/2, whose integral against IG(a0​,b0​) is finite for a0​,b0​>0. At m=n the second mean has its unchanged proper prior distribution as its full conditional distribution. The configuration's posterior probability now has the meaningful interpretation of no change inside the observed sample.

Gaussian change-point Gibbs updates

Words: 75
Gaussian change-point posterior with proper priors OurBigBook.com
For independent means θ∼N(μθ​,tθ​) and ϕ∼N(μϕ​,tϕ​), the first mean's conditional precision is m/v+1/tθ​ and conditional precision-weighted mean is ∑i≤m​xi​/v+μθ​/tθ​; replace m by n−m for the second mean. With v∼IG(a0​,b0​) its conditional law is IG(a0​+n/2,b0​+Sm​/2). The discrete split has conditional probabilities proportional to e−Sm​/(2v). These full conditional distributions give a Gibbs sampler including m=n. Averaging the sampled indicators of that configuration estimates its probability; averaging its conditional probabilities gives an estimate by Rao-Blackwellization.

Poisson change-point posterior (p(θ∣t1​,…,tn​))

Words: 68
Change-point detection OurBigBook.com
For an Inhomogeneous Poisson process whose known positive intensity changes from λ1​ to λ2​ at an unknown time θ∈(0,T), the ordered arrival-time likelihood function is
L(θ)=λ1j(θ)​λ2n−j(θ)​e−λ1​θ−λ2​(T−θ).
(1)
Under a uniform prior, each interval between successive arrivals has an exponential posterior density with rate in the exponent λ2​−λ1​. Its integrated weights allow exact interval selection followed by a truncated exponential draw; when the two rates coincide, the Bayesian posterior is uniform and the data contain no change-time information.

Measurement error

Words: 98 Articles: 1
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
Measurement error is the difference between a recorded variable and the quantity it is intended to measure. It can attenuate associations, create misclassification, and bias nonlinear estimators even when the error has mean zero.

Errors-in-variables model

Words: 64
Measurement error OurBigBook.com
An errors-in-variables model distinguishes a latent true predictor from its noisy measurement and models both the measurement and the response. For example, Wi​∣Ui​∼N(Ui​,s2) and Yi​∣Ui​∼N(a+bUi​,v2), with a population distribution for Ui​, propagate predictor uncertainty into inference on b. Treating Wi​ as exact can create attenuation bias from classical measurement error. Identifiability requires appropriate information about the measurement process or latent predictor distribution.

Regression toward the mean

Words: 42
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
Regression toward the mean is the tendency for units selected because of an extreme noisy measurement to have less extreme subsequent measurements even without an intervention. It follows because the selection captures both a persistent component and an unusually extreme error component.

Sensitivity analysis

Words: 67 Articles: 1
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
A sensitivity analysis examines how conclusions change when assumptions, tuning choices, unidentified parameters, or plausible data perturbations are varied.

Pattern-mixture sensitivity analysis

Words: 48
Sensitivity analysis OurBigBook.com
Specify distributions of measurements separately by observation pattern and vary assumptions about unseen values that the observed data do not identify. For example, shift the imputed binary-response log odds for nonresponders away from its missing at random prediction and refit the substantive analysis. This investigates missing not at random departures rather than testing them from observed data.

Power spectrum

Words: 240 Articles: 5
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
The power spectrum describes how the variance of a random field or stationary process is distributed over spatial wavenumber or temporal frequency.

Spectral tensor (Cij​(k))

Words: 108 Articles: 1
Power spectrum OurBigBook.com
For a statistically homogeneous vector random field, its spectral tensor is the Fourier transform of the componentwise two-point correlation Cij​(r)=E[Bi​(x+r)Bj​(x)]. It distributes cross-correlations between components over wavevectors. With B(k)=∫B(r)e−ik⋅rddr, homogeneity gives E[Bi​(k)Bj​(k′)]=(2π)dδ(k+k′)Cij​(k), understood as an identity of distributions for an infinite stationary field.

Solenoidal isotropic spectral tensor (Cij​=H(k)(δij​−ki​kj​/k2))

Words: 47
Spectral tensor OurBigBook.com
For a statistically homogeneous, isotropic, reflection-symmetric solenoidal vector random field in three dimensions, the nonzero-wavevector spectral tensor is a scalar multiple of the transverse projector of a vector field. Isotropy gives A(k)δij​+D(k)ki​kj​, while zero divergence gives A+Dk2=0. Its trace is 2A, giving the displayed normalization. Without reflection symmetry an additional antisymmetric, helical term can occur.

Statistical homogeneity

Words: 32
Power spectrum OurBigBook.com
A random field is statistically homogeneous when all of its joint distributions are invariant under a common spatial translation of their arguments. Its momentum-space correlation functions consequently contain a Dirac delta function imposing total-momentum conservation.

Statistical isotropy

Words: 78 Articles: 1
Power spectrum OurBigBook.com
A random field is statistically isotropic when all of its joint distributions are invariant under a common spatial rotation of their arguments. A statistically isotropic scalar power spectrum depends only on the magnitude of its wavevector.

Statistical reflection symmetry

Words: 42
Statistical isotropy OurBigBook.com
Statistical reflection symmetry means that the joint distributions of a random field are unchanged by a simultaneous spatial reflection, with each field component transformed according to its vector or pseudovector character. For an isotropic magnetic field, it excludes a parity-odd magnetic helicity contribution to the two-point spectral tensor.

A centered random variable is sub-Gaussian with parameter σ when EetX≤eσ2t2/2 for every real t.

Sub-Gaussian random vector (Ee⟨a,g⟩≤eτ2∥a∥22​/2)

Missing data occur when some intended measurements are unobserved. Whether valid inference can ignore the missingness mechanism depends on how the probability of observation relates to observed and unobserved values.

Item nonresponse leaves a particular measurement unobserved while retaining other measurements on that individual. Unit nonresponse leaves all survey measurements unavailable. Adjusting for an observed auxiliary variable can address item nonresponse under missing at random, but does not identify the auxiliary-variable distribution among unit nonresponders. Extrapolation to them needs further assumptions or external information.

Vary the unobserved outcome probabilities for item and unit nonresponders, and any unknown auxiliary-variable mixture, over scientifically plausible ranges. Recompute the population estimate and identify values at which substantive conclusions change. This probes untestable transport or missing at random assumptions; it is distinct from sampling uncertainty represented by a confidence interval. Letting each missing-outcome probability vary from zero to one gives worst-case identification bounds.

MAR standardization over a fully observed covariate weights within-stratum respondent estimates using covariate frequencies from the whole target cohort.

(20)
For A=m, the unobserved outcome is integrated out, giving ∫fβ​(y)∏j=1m​qj​(y)dy. These probabilities sum to one by telescoping and integration. Dependence of qj​ on y models missing not at random. If all qj​ are independent of y conditional on the regression predictors, the outcome density among responders remains fβ​, as required for complete-case analysis of that conditional model.

Clinical trial OurBigBook.com
Independent trial safety monitoring reviews accumulating serious outcomes according to a prespecified plan and may recommend stopping or modifying a clinical trial when harm or benefit changes the ethical balance. Complete ascertainment of deaths and other severe outcomes is needed even if the trial is sized for a different endpoint. Pooled evidence and prespecified sequential thresholds can make rare-event monitoring useful without presenting a nonsignificant harm comparison as safety.

Clinical equipoise

Words: 56
Clinical trial OurBigBook.com
Clinical equipoise is genuine professional uncertainty about the relative overall benefit and harm of the treatments being compared in a randomized controlled trial. A favorable intermediate endpoint does not by itself resolve uncertainty about mortality. Ethical design requires informed consent, meaningful benefit-risk assessment and monitoring of serious harms; an underpowered safety comparison is not evidence that harm is absent.

Words: 57
Clinical trial OurBigBook.com
A clinical trial comparison must define a common time origin and observation window for both assigned treatments. A probability measured from allocation cannot be replaced by one measured from a later treatment-dependent release or discharge. The latter may describe a different time interval and a selected population. A numerical sample size cannot be obtained by silently treating those probabilities as interchangeable.

Eligibility criteria specify which individuals may enter a clinical trial, defining its enrolled population and excluding individuals for whom the intervention or measurements are unsuitable. Suppose a finite-alphabet transition kernel is uniformly positive and histories agreeing in their most recent r symbols have total variation distance at most br​. Choose decreasing bounds with br​<1 and summable tail. A maximal coupling can be dominated by a match-length chain that increments with probability 1−br​ and resets with probability br​. Its chance of never resetting is ∏r≥0​(1−br​)>0. Successive failed attempts therefore end almost surely, leaving a final infinite run of matches. The dominating chain does not depend on the histories, so future-block laws forget the remote past uniformly. This proves uniqueness of a two-sided law with the prescribed transition kernel without assuming stationarity first.

Last visited vertex of a simple random walk on a cycle (P(L=j)=1/(N−1)(j=0))

Words: 114
Cover time OurBigBook.com
A simple symmetric random walk on a cycle of N≥2 vertices, started at vertex zero, has its last newly visited vertex uniformly distributed on the other N−1 vertices. To prove this for a specified vertex j=0, cut the cycle at j, representing it by a path with absorbing endpoints 0,N both corresponding to j. All other vertices are visited before j exactly when both interior endpoints 1,N−1 are visited before absorption. After the first hit on either interior endpoint, the probability of reaching the other before the adjacent absorbing endpoint is 1/(N−1) by gambler's ruin. The Strong Markov property makes this the desired probability, independent of the original start position. For N=2 the sole unvisited vertex has probability one.

Sum the expected time to expand a random-walk range, 1+2+⋯+(n−1), using linearity of expectation; no independence of expansion times is needed.

Ancillary statistic OurBigBook.com
A maximal ancillary statistic has no strictly finer ancillary partition of the sample space, but different maximal ancillary partitions can exist. Let (U,V) take values in {0,1}2, with probabilities θ/2 on each equal pair and (1−θ)/2 on each unequal pair, for 0<θ<1. Both U and V have the Bernoulli distribution with success probability 1/2 for every θ. Their joint law depends on θ, so combining them is not ancillary. Each partition is maximal: splitting one of its two-point cells singles out a point whose probability depends on θ. There is no common ancillary refinement, and conditioning on one ancillary choice need not specify a unique conditioning principle for all models.

For a parameter of interest ψ and nuisance parameter λ, a partial ancillary for ψ has a marginal law independent of ψ, possibly depending on λ. This differs from a fully ancillary statistic, whose law is independent of both. For independent Poisson counts with means λψ and λ(1−ψ), their total is Poisson with mean λ, while the first count conditional on the total is binomial with success probability ψ. Conditioning on the total eliminates λ. A partial ancillary does not automatically eliminate a nuisance parameter; the conditional law must actually be free of that parameter.

A complete sufficient statistic is independent of every ancillary statistic. To prove this, let S be complete and sufficient, let A be ancillary, and take any bounded measurable function h. By sufficiency, g(S)=Eθ​[h(A)∣S] has a parameter-independent version; by ancillarity, c=Eθ​h(A) is independent of θ. Thus Eθ​[g(S)−c]=0 for every θ. Completeness gives g(S)=c almost surely. Choosing h to be the indicator of each measurable event in the ancillary space proves independence. Combining the prime-power periods by the Chinese remainder theorem gives period M. For M=12k=22k3k, the multiplier criterion reduces to a≡1(mod12), together with gcd(c,6)=1. Words: 80
Minimum-variance combination of unbiased sample means OurBigBook.com
Split independent observational blocks into two folds. Use one fold to estimate the combination weight for the two sample means in the other fold, and conversely. Each held-out combination is an unbiased estimator conditionally on its training fold because its two held-out sample means have the same expectation. A deterministic average of the two combinations remains unbiased. Under consistency of the moment estimates and balanced fold sizes, the weights approach those of the minimum-variance combination of unbiased sample means. Paired observations must stay together when splitting or bootstrapping so their covariance is preserved.

Linear least squares

Words: 62 Articles: 2
Probability and statistics OurBigBook.com
Linear least squares minimizes ∥Ax−b∥2 over a vector x. Its normal equations for linear least squares are ATAx=ATb; geometrically Ax is the orthogonal projection of b onto the range of A.

Linear least-squares projection

Words: 39 Articles: 1
Linear least squares OurBigBook.com
This is an orthogonal projection interpretation of linear least squares. The best affine predictor has slope covariance divided by predictor variance and intercept chosen to match means.

Schur complement covariance

Words: 15
Linear least-squares projection OurBigBook.com
The residual variance after projection onto one factor is Var(Y)−Cov(X,Y)2/Var(X), a covariance Schur complement.
